title: Gafgyt_Botnet_Investigation_199
description: Investigate and identify the source of unusual traffic patterns and performance degradation in the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and performance degradation. Your task is to investigate and identify the source of these issues.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Use the following credentials to access the bot1 host via SSH:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that is periodically communicating with an external host? Submit the service name.
levels.solution: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services. The suspicious service is likely named `bot-beacon.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that might be responsible for external communication.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services and identify the suspicious one.

levels.title: Identify Network Flooding Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service that is generating high volumes of network traffic? Submit the service name.
levels.solution: Examine the systemd services and look for any services that might be responsible for network flooding. The service is likely named `bot-flood.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the systemd services and look for any services that might be responsible for network flooding.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that might be generating high volumes of network traffic.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services and identify the network flooding service.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the name of the timer unit that ensures the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot? Submit the timer unit name.
levels.solution: Look for systemd timer units that might be responsible for starting the suspicious service. The timer unit is likely named `bot-beacon.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for systemd timer units that might be responsible for starting the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd timers and look for any unusual or recently created timers.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers and identify the persistence mechanism.
